---
title: "Notation and conventions"
---

## Coordinates, clocks, and units {#sec-notation}

| Symbol | Meaning and convention |
|---|---|
| $\mathbf q$ | Uniform-mass Lagrangian comoving label |
| $\mathbf x=\mathbf q+\boldsymbol\Psi$ | Current comoving position; kept unwrapped in geometry |
| $a$ | Scale factor, the PM integration clock |
| $D$ | Linear growth, equal to $a$ in EdS; early-time $D\sim a$ convention in the inherited $\Lambda$CDM core |
| $\mathbf u=a\dot{\mathbf x}$ | Physical peculiar velocity; dot here denotes cosmic time |
| $\mathbf v_D=\partial\mathbf x/\partial D$ | Derivative used by the LPT core; not physical peculiar velocity |
| $\mathbf v_a=\partial(\mathbf x/L)/\partial a$ | Phase-space panel velocity in unit-box coordinates |
| $\mathbf p=a^2\dot{\mathbf x}$ | Canonical momentum; $a^3E(a)\partial\mathbf x/\partial a$ with $H_0=1$ |
| $F_{ij}=\delta_{ij}+\Psi_{i,j}$ | Deformation gradient |
| $J=\det F$, $J_T$ | Spectral-vertex Jacobian and affine-simplex signed volume ratio |
| $r=1+\delta=\rho/\bar\rho$ | Dimensionless positive total density; stream contributions use absolute volume |
| $L,N_q,N_e$ | Box side, vertices per axis, Eulerian cells per axis |
| $R_f,R_s$ | Initial-condition filter scale and observable filter scale |
| $A$ | Amplitude multiplier of the initial field; tangent at $A=1$ |
| $y=\log_{10}r$ | PDF coordinate; ordinate is probability per unit $y$ |
| $V_B=L^d$, $M_B=\bar\rho V_B$ | Box volume and total mass |
| $p_{VV},p_{MV},p_{VM},p_{MM}$ | Joint density PDFs at fixed displacement; subscripts specify endpoint measures |
| $\xi(\mathbf s)$ | Volume average of $\delta(\mathbf x)\delta(\mathbf x+\mathbf s)$ at a fixed epoch |
| $K_{TU}(\mathbf s)$, $q_{TU}(\mathbf s)$ | Periodic overlap volume and normalized displacement PDF of two uniform element points |
| $\mathbf c_T$, $\Sigma_T$, $W_T(\mathbf k)$ | Unwrapped element centroid, spatial covariance, and centered Fourier form factor |

The facade uses unit-box positions and $H_0=1$ internally, with an explicit physical box length in $h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$; @sec-dimensional-units gives the conversions. Fourier output uses physical $k$ and $P_d$. The live Gaussian observation filter uses $R_s/L$ as its control; the initial filter is entered directly in $h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$. Neither Gaussian filter is the archival top-hat filter. Lower-dimensional modes describe translationally invariant solutions, with a distinct power normalization.

## Fourier and finite-element conventions

The forward FFT is unnormalized, the inverse FFT includes $1/N_e^d$, and a Fourier integral mode includes $1/L^d$. Reported power uses @eq-fourier-power. The zero density-contrast mode is zero. Odd spectral derivative operators suppress an even-grid Nyquist component to retain a real derivative field; the Poisson magnitude retains its full wavevector norm.

Array storage is row major with the last spatial index fastest; positions and velocities are interleaved by component. Every square is split along the same diagonal; every cube has six Kuhn tetrahedra. A boundary neighbor receives a periodic lift before constructing an element. The term “P0” refers to a constant density inside the affine simplex; “P1” refers to an additional normalized linear density reconstruction.

Mass-weighted smoothed PDFs use unsmoothed mass weights as defined in @eq-mass-environment. Hard histogram ranges are finite; captured probabilities are reported. The continuous derivative panel is P0 Fourier power, not a histogram or an exact-clipping derivative.

Two independently mass-selected positions conditioned on their displacement use the pair normalization $1+\xi$, as in @eq-pair-change-measure. Their conditioned density marginals generally differ from the one-point mass PDF. Centroid differences describe unwrapped element pairs; periodic overlap kernels determine their exact displacement distributions. Volumes alone do not specify simplex shape in two or three dimensions.

The compensated GPU finite-difference observer in @sec-gpu-fd uses
$F_\pm=F[\mathbf x(A\pm h)]$, $\Delta F=F_+-F_-$ and $h=10^{-4}$.
Its auxiliary path parameter $\theta\in[-1,1]$ joins these endpoint geometries:
$\mathbf c_j$ is the midpoint and $\mathbf b_j$ their half-gap. The symbol $M$
in that section bounds the absolute phase slope along this path, rather than a
particle mass. For the local divided-difference series, $c$ is the knot count,
$\beta_j$ a centered angular phase, and $e_r,h_m,g_m$ are elementary symmetric,
complete homogeneous and factorial-normalized coefficients, respectively.

For adaptive GPU series truncation in @eq-gpu-adaptive-tail, $R=\sum_j|\beta_j|$ is an angular knot radius and $K$ is the highest retained coefficient order. These are local numerical parameters, distinct from the physical filter scales $R_f,R_s$. GPU exact-deposit output is $r=\rho/\bar\rho$, so global unit mass means the arithmetic cell mean of $r$ is one.
